description: The bar chart illustrates average accuracy (labeled as “Average Performance”) across 11 datasets for five training methods, with the method categories shown along the horizontal axis in the order Standard, Self-RAG, FactTune, ClInGS (w/), and ClInGS, and the numeric performance values shown on the vertical axis. The y-axis is labeled “Average Performance” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 60 with tick marks at 10-unit intervals. There are five single (non-stacked, non-grouped) vertical bars: Standard is colored orange and reaches a little above 50 (approximately 52), Self-RAG is beige and is just above 50 (approximately 53), FactTune is light green and is slightly above 50 (approximately 51–52), ClInGS (w/) is light blue and is around the mid-50s (approximately 53–54), and ClInGS is dark blue and is the tallest bar, reaching just under 60 (approximately 59). The bars are not shown as sorted by value (they follow the listed method order), and there are no visible annotations, outlines, or other emphasis beyond distinct bar colors.
caption_used: Average accuracy across 11 datasets (y-axis) for each training method (x-axis). The bar chart depicts the performance of five distinct methods: Standard, Self-RAG, FactTune, ClInGS (w/), and ClInGS. The vertical axis, labeled 'Average Performance,' spans from 0 to 60 in 10-unit increments. The Standard method (orange) achieves approximately 52, while Self-RAG (beige) stabilizes at a slightly lower value of 48. FactTune (light green) consistently exceeds Self-RAG with a performance of roughly 55. ClInGS (w/) (light blue) marginally surpasses FactTune at about 53, whereas ClInGS (blue) demonstrates a marked improvement, reaching nearly 58. Notably, Self-RAG and FactTune exhibit minimal performance divergence, suggesting comparable efficacy between these two approaches.
